title: End-of-Support for SMS OTP Authentication in Authentication Service

blocks.text: As of August 07, 2026, Authentication Service will no longer support SMS-based one-time passcodes (OTP) for multi-factor authentication (MFA) for hosted users and hosted admins. This change strengthens Authentication Service's MFA posture as per the NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-63B guidance, which classifies SMS or voice delivered over the public switched telephone network (PSTN) as a RESTRICTED method for out-of-band authentication.
To learn more, see NIST SP 800-63B §5.1.3.3 - Authentication using the Public Switched Telephone Network and NIST SP 800-63B §5.2.10 - Restricted Authenticators.

table: SMS MFA enrollment will no longer be available for new tenants created post the announcement date. Existing admins and users already using SMS MFA are not impacted at this stage. These admins and users will be prompted to choose another available MFA method.
SMS MFA will be disabled for sign-in. Admins and users attempting to use SMS will be guided to set up another available MFA method during sign-in.

blocks.text: Make sure that all the impacted admins and users in your organization have transitioned to another available MFA method before August 07, 2026, to avoid any disruption during sign-in.
If you have additional questions, contact Zscaler Support.
